classification.difficultyReason: Convert tonnes to kilograms, model two weighted loads, select elimination multipliers and interpret the man mass; familiar prescribed simultaneous modelling.

content.prompt:
Solve by introducing two pronumerals and forming two simultaneous equations, even though this problem may be done more easily using one pronumeral.

An army transport vehicle has a carrying capacity of 5 tonnes. It can be used to transport either 20 men and 17 pieces of equipment or 35 men and 11 pieces of equipment. How many kilograms does each man weigh? (Assume that all men have the same weight and all pieces of equipment have the same weight.)

answer.worked:
Let $x$ be the mass of each man in kilograms and $y$ the mass of each piece of equipment in kilograms. Taking each stated load to fill the capacity, $5$ tonnes is $5000$ kg.

$$\begin{align*}20x+17y&=5000&&\text{(1)}\\35x+11y&=5000&&\text{(2)}\end{align*}$$

Multiply equation (1) by 11 and equation (2) by 17:

$$\begin{align*}220x+187y&=55000&&\text{(3)}\\595x+187y&=85000&&\text{(4)}\end{align*}$$

Subtract equation (3) from equation (4):

$$\begin{align*}375x&=30000\\x&=80\end{align*}$$

Substitute $x=80$ into equation (1):

$$\begin{align*}20(80)+17y&=5000\\17y&=3400\\y&=200\end{align*}$$

Each man weighs $80$ kg. Check: $20(80)+17(200)=5000$ and $35(80)+11(200)=5000$.
